title: Mercurys Boot & Baal Bone Gap
lede: A short but steep walk through thick scrub to a boot-shaped rock on the Capertee cliffline, which you can climb from the toe.
description: A short, steep, partly off-track walk through scrub to Mercurys Boot, a boot-shaped sandstone rock on the Capertee cliffline near Baal Bone Gap in Gardens of Stone National Park.
hero_alt: A bushwalker standing on top of Mercurys Boot, a boot-shaped sandstone rock on the Capertee cliffline

card.image_alt: A walker on top of Mercurys Boot
card.blurb: A short but steep walk through thick scrub to a boot-shaped rock on the Capertee cliffline. Climb it from the toe.

facts.label: Region
facts.value: Capertee Valley rim, near Ben Bullen

facts.label: Distance
facts.value: About 1.6 km one way from the Moffitts Trail ridge; under 500 m from Baal Bone Gap

facts.label: Walk type
facts.value: Partly off-track; Return, or loop back via the fire trail

intro: High above the Capertee Valley, a great sandstone block leans out over the drop. From the right angle it looks just like a boot. It's a short walk, but a steep one, with lots of scrub and some rock scrambling, and you can climb right up onto the Boot from the toe.

getting_there.intro: There are two ways in: along the ridge from Moffitts Trail (about 1.6 km), or up from Baal Bone Gap (under 500 m, but very steep). Both involve scrub and some rock scrambling.

options.heading: Moffitts Trail ridge
options.text:
Head for Moffitts Trail (also signposted as Ben Bullen Trail) and leave it on the ridge at Ben Bullen GR 284 189. Conventional vehicles should stop wherever the track starts to look too rough for them.

From the ridge it's about 1.6 km to the Boot. Bushbash out to the cliffline and follow it to the Boot.

options.heading: Baal Bone Gap
options.text: Baal Bone Gap is a natural break in the cliffs just below the Boot. It's under 500 m from the Gap to the Boot, but it's very steep, with lots of scrub and some rock scrambling up through the cliffs.

getting_there.note: Fire trail conditions change quickly after rain. Check the current NPWS alerts for Gardens of Stone National Park before you go.

walk_intro: There's no formed track to the Boot. Expect steep ground, thick scrub, high cliffs and some rock scrambling, with the cliffline as your guide.

stops.heading: Moffitts Trail or Baal Bone Gap
stops.text: Start from the ridge off Moffitts Trail (Ben Bullen GR 284 189), or from Baal Bone Gap. Either way, head for the cliff edge above the Capertee Valley.

stops.heading: Bushbash to the cliffline
stops.text: Whichever way you come, expect lots of scrub. From Baal Bone Gap it's very steep, with some rock scrambling through the cliffs. Once you reach the cliffline, follow it and the views open up over the Capertee Valley.

stops.heading: Mercurys Boot
stops.text:
You'll know the Boot when you see it: a big rock jutting out over the valley, shaped unmistakably like a boot.

You can climb onto it from the toe. Take care on top, because it's a long way down on the valley side. And make sure you get a kicking picture before you leave.
stops.image_alt: A walker standing on top of Mercurys Boot against a clear blue sky
stops.caption: Standing on top of Mercurys Boot, high above the Capertee Valley

stops.heading: Back to the car
stops.text: Retrace your steps the way you came, or make a loop by returning to your car along the fire trail.

map.alt: Topographic map showing the routes to Mercurys Boot from Moffitts Trail and from Baal Bone Gap
map.caption: Approximate route in orange. Base map: Ben Bullen 8931-4S topographic map.

tips.heading: Off-track navigation
tips.text: There's no track or signs to the Boot. Carry a map and compass or GPS, and know how to use them.

tips.heading: Cliff edges
tips.text: The cliffs are high and sheer, and the edges can be undercut. There's some rock scrambling on the way, so take care climbing the Boot and keep well back from the edge, especially with children or in wind.

tips.heading: Water
tips.text: Don't count on finding any. There may be water in a pipe at Baal Bone Gap, but the tap may be locked, so carry all you'll need.

tips.heading: Respect the Country
tips.text: Baal Bone Gap has Aboriginal cultural sites, including hand stencils. Look, but don't touch. Leave no trace.

tips.heading: Tell someone
tips.text: Leave your plans with someone, and think about carrying a PLB. There's very little phone coverage out there.
